This is pure text-to-image (no ControlNet/IPAdapter installed) -- style/character consistency across future generations (player frames, enemies, bosses, biomes, UI) comes from reusing this same checkpoint + reusing this prompt's descriptive language/palette, not from image-conditioning on the reference PNG.

The approved reference image intentionally does NOT depict the gilded eye-mask on the main figure -- 5 generation rounds plus 1 inpaint attempt showed mask-presence and full-body/correct-limb framing consistently traded off against each other in this model at this resolution. A separate mask-study inset appears in the same image but is NOT face-consistent with the main figure (SDXL invented it as a 'concept sheet' embellishment, not a true multi-view of one identity) -- treat it as a loose design study only, not a locked identity reference.

Design decision: the mask becomes a separate in-game item/toggle with its own gameplay mechanics (see project backlog), not a fixed part of Abhimanyu's default appearance. Future frame-generation prompts should describe the mask explicitly (e.g. 'wearing a small ornate gilded mask over his eyes') only when generating the masked-form sprite variant.

Prior rounds (not kept): v1 single-image collage (weak Indian motifs, no distinct views); v2 three independent bust crops (back view failed -- came out front-facing); v3 front/side/back with mask emphasis 1.6 (overcorrected to extreme mask closeup) and a genuine side-profile bust (no legs); v4 front (correct dhoti/sword, cropped at thighs, no mask) + true side profile bust (no mask, no legs).
